analysis:
Examined base text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 1-1017) plus the patch excerpt. The head side was only partially visible (the patch excerpt is truncated), so the changes after the first two hunks were not checked.

Observed changes:
- A new fail-closed guard at head ~512-519 rejects GLM5 media requests that need withheld output, i.e. required/named tool_choice or JSON response_format. It calls releaseBox.fire() before throwing, so the model reservation is not leaked. It runs before any decode, vision reservation or tower work. This narrows behavior, since previously unsupported combinations are refused earlier, and I see no new attack surface.
- At ~985-1006 the text path computes withholdsGLMOutput and ORs it into the nativeReasoningPrefix selection. This makes GLM reasoning a typed channel when output is withheld. It affects only output parsing and reasoning/content separation. The patch shows no path where plaintext bypasses validation, encryption or the withholding handler. Encryption of the SSE chunks (T-008) sits downstream in ProviderLoop and is not touched in the visible hunks.
- Prefix-cache scoping (T-041) is unchanged in the visible hunks. cacheScope, cacheEnabled, requestCacheScope and donationDemand still flow to bridge.submitTokenized as in base.
- The other changed ranges (head 1126, 1153, 1187, 1231-1241, 1300-1309, 1419, 1470, 1490-1493, 1590-1598) fall in lines I could not see, either because they are beyond the supplied base text or because the patch is truncated. I cannot assess them.

Remaining questions for integration:
- Whether GLM5NextPromptPolicy.withholdsOutput is deterministic and pure, and where it is defined.
- Whether the unseen head hunks in prepareNativeMiMoMedia and in the stream helpers preserve release-token firing and deadline checks.
- Whether the native reasoning router handles a GLM-supplied "<think></think>" fallback prefix correctly.

No concrete security regression is identified in the visible evidence.
